title: Completeness of the BLR linearity test
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be linear, meaning that $f(x \oplus y) = f(x) \oplus f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$. Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ equals $1$; that is, when $x$ and $y$ are drawn uniformly and independently from $\{0,1\}^n$, the test always accepts.
hypotheses_covered: f maps the Boolean hypercube of dimension n to Bool
f is linear: f(x XOR y) = f(x) XOR f(y) for all x, y
replaced:
If $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ is linear, then
$\texttt{BoolBLR.BLR\_accept\_prob}\,f = 1$; that is, the BLR test accepts
every linear function with probability $1$.
